title: Three Ways Recorder
context: Grade 5, the math lab page that closes the chapter. An adult sees a class chart of measurements. What the page is doing is bringing every idea of the chapter to real measures: writing each one three ways, ordering them in one unit, and adding them.

writeup.why: Write one real measure in two units, in its smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit, put a group's measures in order in one unit, add a group's weights, and measure the water a group drinks with a measuring jug.
writeup.look: A class record chart with a row for each child, record cards that flip through three forms, and a measuring jug marked in millilitres.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Three Ways Recorder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of measures recorded. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The class record chart fills the left of the area from x 90 to x 760: five rows, one for each child of the group, each 72 tall from y 250, under a header row at y 210 with columns for a long jump, a school bag's weight and a drink of water, and a total row at y 620. The record card stands at x 800, y 230, 300 by 110, with the measure in deep blue, labelled Given, and the Flip button under it at x 800, y 360. Each flip shows the card's next form in green, labelled Same measure, with a violet Unit fact beside it and a grey zero, labelled Place holder, wherever a place is held open. A row being dragged is amber. On the third phase the total row fills in green, labelled Answer. On the fourth phase the measuring jug stands at x 820, y 420, 160 wide and 260 tall, its marks and numbers in near-black ink, and each drink poured from it is read off its marks and entered in the water column. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key, a delete key, and a key for each unit in use. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. The measure the question gives, in the unit it is given in, is deep blue, labelled Given or Measure. The measure the working reaches, and a reading on a scale, is green, labelled Answer, Reading or Same measure. The places moved across the unit chart, and the worth of one small mark on a scale, are vermilion, labelled Move or One mark. A unit fact, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet, labelled Unit fact, Unit or Other scale. The part taken away, and a part left over after sharing, are rose, labelled Taken away or Left over. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open inside a number, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. Rulers, tapes, jugs, scales, thermometer tubes, chart lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The group's chart stays up, every row in order, every card showing all three forms, and the totals in green.

phases.win: the three forms stand side by side, all green, all one jump
phases.does: flips the card and types each form in turn
phases.goal: one measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit
phases.says: Flip it. Say the same jump another way.
phases.check: Away from the screen: say your own height in metres and centimetres, then in centimetres.
phases.feels: three different-looking forms standing side by side, all green, all one jump
phases.hands: Measure a jump on the playground with a tape, write it in metres and centimetres, then in centimetres, then as a decimal in metres, on three sides of one folded card.
phases.tries: First rung: write only the smallest-unit form. Second rung: write it as a decimal in metres. Third rung: the same task on a jump with no empty place, before the question's own jump returns.

phases.screen: a long jump entered on a record card in metres and centimetres

phases.goal: put every measure in one unit, then order them

phases.screen: four jumps on the chart, each written in a different form

phases.win: the total turns green, in grams, in kilograms and grams, and as a decimal

wrong.screen: the child's total stays, and beside it the thousand millilitres are bundled into one litre in steps

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, as the last drink is entered, the water column of the chart fills like a glass from the bottom up, and the total lands at the top in litres and millilitres.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet recorded. On the first phase a long jump sits on a record card in metres and centimetres with the Flip button beside it. On the second four jumps sit on the chart, each written in a different form. On the third three weights sit on the chart in kilograms and grams above an empty total row. On the fourth a measuring jug marked in millilitres stands beside the water column of the chart. One thing moves, once: the Flip button, the first row, or the jug gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any measures the group takes, entered on cards, flipped through three forms, ordered and added. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on writing a measure three ways, ordering, adding weights and measuring water.

observations.why: a measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit, or as a decimal in the larger unit.
observations.soWhat: choose the form that suits the job: one unit to compare, the smallest unit to add.
observations.observe: The three forms on the card looked different but were all one jump.

observations.why: measures in one unit can be compared by their numbers alone.
observations.soWhat: put every measure in one unit, then order them.
observations.observe: The rows only fell into a clear order once every jump was in centimetres.

observations.why: adding whole numbers in the smallest unit needs no carrying across units.

observations.why: the jug is marked in millilitres.
observations.soWhat: a measuring jug turns a drink of water into a measure that can be added.
observations.observe: Each drink read off the jug's marks was a real measure, not a guess.

source_tool.description: A class record chart fills the working area, one row for each child of a group of five, with columns for a long jump, a school bag's weight and a drink of water. A measure the question gives, or one the group has taken, is entered on a record card in deep blue, labelled Given. A Flip button turns the card through three forms: in two units, in the smallest unit, and as a decimal in the larger unit, each form green, labelled Same measure, with a violet unit fact beside it and a grey zero, labelled Place holder, wherever a place is held open. On the second phase the rows are dragged into ascending order once every measure shows in one unit, the row being moved amber. On the third the weights are added in the smallest unit and the total is written back in the larger unit, green, labelled Answer. On the fourth a measuring jug marked in millilitres stands beside the chart, and each drink is poured out of it, read off its marks and entered, then added into litres and millilitres. The running count at the top left of the canvas counts the measures recorded.
source_tool.art_direction: A class record chart on the wall / Picture book

style.text: Least text. One header line, short labels, nothing else. The voice carries the teaching and the caption carries the voice.

stage.note: Every coordinate is authored in 1600x900, so a smartboard and a phone in landscape get one composition. Nothing scrolls. The three bands below are the settled layout, taken from Two Hundred Trail in Class 3 chapter 3 once it was finished; a tool that has to depart from one of them says in its own writeup.stage which band it changed and why.

bands.canvas: 92 to 746. One rounded panel holding everything the child works on.
bands.footer: 758 to 900. The voice at the far left, the phase bar at the right.
bands.header: 0 to 80. One line, and only one.

zones.bar: the phase bar at the right of the footer, the question count under it
zones.pad: under the slot, and furniture on every phase: twelve keys three across where a number is asked for, a word pad where a name or a rule is
zones.name: the tool name at the far left of the header, a measured dot set clear of it
zones.runs: the running count, on the canvas at its top left, never up in the chrome. It counts the thing the tool is actually building; where a tool has nothing to count that corner carries the record being kept instead, and that tool's own stage says so
zones.slot: the question and the child's answer, fixed down the right of the canvas
zones.work: the working area, one thousand and eighty-six by five hundred and twenty-eight
zones.title: the phase title beside that dot, on the same single header line
zones.voice: the caption at the far left of the footer, its speaking dot beside it
zones.chrome: again, sound and restart, as round controls at the far right of the header

stage.furniture: The working area is furnished from the first frame. What waits for the child is the count, not the picture: the panels, the slot and the pad are all up and empty before anything is asked.
stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare, because the working area is the tool.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box anywhere on the stage. The score leaves on the finished event and it is the host that decides whether to show it, so a child working is never watching a number that judges them.

style.motion: Animate only what carries meaning. Anything that is not changing does not move. Every reward is the maths itself moving, never confetti. Honour prefers-reduced-motion.
drawing: Hand-built inline SVG. No assets and no network, so a school cart works offline.
Chunky rounded forms and large touch targets. A finger is the pointer, not a mouse.

Drawn things, not abstract boxes: a unit chart of seven columns from kilo to milli with the base unit in the middle, rulers and tapes marked in their units, kitchen scales, measuring jugs marked in millilitres, and thermometers with labelled marks.
Every measure is written with its unit on every line, and every decimal names the unit it is in, so 3.04 L is never shown as a bare 3.04.
Every mixed measure shown is ordinary: its smaller part is less than one of the larger unit.
Places are counted from the unit the child has to the unit the child wants, one hop at a time, and each hop shows the number, not the unit, divided or multiplied by 10.
Multiplying and dividing a measure happen in its smallest unit, in whole numbers, and a sharing that does not come out even shows what is left over.
A thermometer shows what one small mark is worth before its column is read, and a Celsius reading sits beside a Fahrenheit one only in the four pairs the chapter prints.
Nothing is animated except the one thing being explained: a hop across the chart, a carry across units, a length shared into equal pieces, or a column rising to a mark.
style.palette_rule: A chrome colour never fills a number, a unit or a mark the child is reading, and a content colour is never used for chrome. This chapter colours the roles a measure plays in a piece of working: the measure the question gives is deep blue, and the measure the working reaches, with a reading taken off a scale, is green; those two are the same two in every tool and every picture of this chapter. The places moved across the unit chart, each one dividing or multiplying the number by 10, and the worth of one small mark on a scale are vermilion. A unit fact such as 1 kg = 1000 g, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet. The part taken away, and a remainder left over after sharing, are rose. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey. Each role is named in writing first, with the words Given, Answer, Move, Unit fact, Taken away, Left over and Place holder, so the stage still reads with the colour taken away.

rules: Every spoken line is also printed in the caption line at the far left of the footer, so a muted tablet and a child who cannot hear lose nothing.
The caption stays in the footer. Nothing is ever written over the working area.

Numbers are written as words in every line and never as digits, so the voice says four steps and not 4 steps. Handed a digit, a synthesiser reads it in whatever register it likes and the chapter loses the words it is teaching.
The voice never gives the answer. It asks the same question a different way.
It speaks on opening, once when a phase begins, on a miss, and at the finish. It is silent otherwise; a tool that chatters gets muted, and then the first rule is all that is left.
props.muted is honoured at the source, and turning sound off cancels any line already speaking.
voice.where: The caption line sits at the far left of the footer with a small dot beside it that glows while the voice is talking. An again control repeats the last line.
voice.figure: None. The voice speaks with nothing on the stage.
voice.onMiss: Flip the card through all three forms. Do they all say the same measure?
voice.onNext: A new measure for the chart. Record it the same way.
voice.opening: A class record chart, with a card to fill in.
voice.onFinish: You wrote real measures three ways, put them in order and added them.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Record any measure and flip it through its forms.
voice.figure_rule: A figure appears only where the printed chapter puts one and it has work to do. Everywhere else the voice speaks from the caption line with nothing on the stage: a mascot with no job is one more thing competing with the quantities the child is looking at.
voice.voicePreference: an English voice, female where one is offered

placement.where: After the group has taken its long jumps with a measuring tape, weighed its school bags on a kitchen scale and poured its drinks from a measuring jug. The tool is where those real measures are written three ways, ordered and added.

answer_key.rule: One measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit, or as a decimal in the larger unit, and all three are right when the question does not name a form. Put every measure in one unit before ordering. Add weights in the smallest unit and write the total back in the larger unit. Measure each drink of water with a measuring jug, add the millilitres, and write the total in litres and millilitres.
answer_key.wrong: The stage keeps what the child entered. A card flipped to a wrong form stays, and the other two forms are laid beside it so the one that differs stands out, lit amber. A row dragged out of order stays, and its measure is shown in the chart's one unit beside its neighbours. Nothing is cleared and nothing is marked.

hostProps.muted: Sound off. Honour it at the source, not by muting an element later. The captions carry on.
hostProps.phase: number, 1-based, which phase to build. The host chooses the activity; the component builds that phase and nothing else and never moves on by itself.
hostProps.device: tablet / web / smartboard. The stage is a fixed 1600x900 that scales; lay nothing out per device.
hostProps.audience: classroom or solo, and ACCEPTED AND NOT ACTED ON. The teach run and the hint ladder run either way. Kept so the contract is one shape across the book, and named here so nobody reads the shape as a promise.
hostProps.learnQuestions: The four worked items, one per phase, supplied by the host.
hostProps.practiceQuestions: The eight practice items, supplied by the host.

phase_mount.run: A phase is a complete activity in itself and it runs once. The teaching and the doing are not two screens and not two modes: the stage is furnished once, the voice talks over it, and the child starts working on the same stage without anything being rebuilt. Whatever the tool as a whole has to say goes into the FIRST phase's teach run, because there is no opening screen to say it on.
phase_mount.idle: NO AUTO-ADVANCE. After firing, the tool goes idle on the settled phase with the child's work still on it, and stops. Where the host supplies onNext it is drawn and it calls the host back; nothing in the component advances a phase.
phase_mount.prop: phase: number, 1-based, matching writeup.phases[].n. Rounded, clamped, and defaulting to 1 when the host sends nothing, so a bare mount is still a working tool rather than a blank screen. Read once: changing which phase a mount shows is a re-mount.
phase_mount.rule: ONE PHASE, ONE MOUNT. The host says which phase to build by passing `phase`, and the component builds that phase and nothing else. It does not know what came before it and it never moves on by itself.
phase_mount.opening: There is no opening panel and no Start button. The host has already chosen the activity, and a cover screen in front of it is a click between a child and the work. writeup.opening is the first frame of every mount rather than a panel of its own.
phase_mount.completion: The terminal event `finished`, with the phase in its detail, fired exactly once and guarded by a one-shot ref that only a restart re-arms, with the chime and the settle OUTSIDE the guard. props.onComplete is called alongside it: the event is the platform's signal and the callback is the host wrapper's, and firing only one of them leaves a child on a tool that never completes.
phase_mount.notInAMount: No finish card and no free play. Both are the host's now, built out of what the events told it. writeup.finish and writeup.freePlay stay as the record of what they are.

shared_state.note: What getState() returns. These names are a contract: the host reads them to persist and resume a child mid-activity, so renaming one breaks resume. `mode` is gone from this list because there is no mode. `phase` is the phase the host mounted, so a resume restores the work inside a phase and the host restores which phase.

agent_control.reason: Every tool in this chapter is child-operated. There is no agent-driven Concept mode, no postMessage command channel and no narration the tool waits on; the adult, where there is one, talks over the tool rather than through it.

steps: 100 cm make 1 m, so 3 m is 300 cm.
Add the 7 cm: 300 + 7 = 307, so 3 m 7 cm is 307 cm.
As a decimal in metres, 7 cm is 0.07 m, with a zero holding the tenths place.
So 3 m 7 cm is 307 cm, which is 3.07 m.
items.question: A long jump measures 3 m 7 cm. Write it in centimetres, and as a decimal in metres.
items.checkpoint: One measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit.
items.misconception: Leaving out the zero that holds the tenths place, which makes the jump longer than it was.

steps: Write all four in centimetres: 215 cm, 250 cm, 208 cm and 251 cm.
Ascending order goes from smallest to largest.
So the order is 208 cm, 2 m 15 cm, 2.5 m, 2 m 51 cm.
items.question: Four jumps measure 2 m 15 cm, 2.5 m, 208 cm and 2 m 51 cm. Put them in ascending order.
items.checkpoint: Put every measure in one unit, then order them.
items.misconception: Reading 2.5 m as 2 m 5 cm, which puts that jump first instead of third.

steps: Write each in grams: 1640 g, 2085 g and 1900 g.
1000 g make 1 kg, so 5625 g is 5 kg 625 g.
As a decimal in kilograms, 5 kg 625 g is 5.625 kg.
items.question: Three bags of fruit weigh 1 kg 640 g, 2 kg 85 g and 1 kg 900 g. What do they weigh together?
items.checkpoint: Add weights in the smallest unit, then write the total back in the larger unit.
items.misconception: Writing 2 kg 85 g as if it were 2 kg 850 g, which adds grams that are not there.

steps: Each drink is read off a measuring jug marked in millilitres.
1000 mL make 1 litre, so 1150 mL is 1 L 150 mL.
As a decimal in litres, 1 L 150 mL is 1.15 L.
items.question: Five children drink 210 mL, 235 mL, 190 mL, 260 mL and 255 mL of water, each poured from a measuring jug. How much is that in litres and millilitres?
items.checkpoint: Measure each drink with a measuring jug, add the millilitres, then write the total in litres.
items.misconception: Guessing each drink by eye instead of reading a measuring jug, so the total cannot be trusted.

learn.shape: Worked items, shown solved, mandatory before practice unlocks.
learn.selection: Fixed order, walking the phases from the first to the last.
learn.content_criterion: One per phase, so Learn walks the whole topic and stops.

items.question: A packet's label says 1 kg 250 g. Write the weight in grams.
Write 4 m 60 cm as a decimal in metres.
Before putting the jumps of a group in order, what must you do first?
items.final_answer: Write all of them in one unit

items.question: Put in ascending order: 1 kg 80 g, 1 kg 800 g, 1008 g.
Two bags weigh 2 kg 450 g and 1 kg 675 g. What do they weigh together, in grams?
Why is a measuring jug used for the water each child drinks?
items.final_answer: It is marked in millilitres, so each drink can be read, not guessed

items.question: Three parcels weigh 850 g, 1 kg 20 g and 1.3 kg. What is their total, as a decimal in kilograms?
Four cups hold 325 mL, 410 mL, 195 mL and 290 mL. How much is that altogether, in litres and millilitres?

practice.selection: Fixed order, easy first, and every phase represented.
practice.interaction_rules: Answered on the tool itself. A wrong answer returns the question with a hint; nothing is marked and retries are unlimited.

student_controls.effect: takes a measure the group has taken or a label gives
turns the card through its three forms
moves a row of the chart into order
pours a drink out of a measuring jug marked in millilitres
types a measure, a form or a total

teaching_notes: Write every measurement three ways: in two units, in the smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit. Put all the measures in one unit before ordering them. Use a measuring jug or a marked bottle for the water step, and order the capacities too. Weigh bags or books rather than children, so nobody's weight is read aloud. Enter the measures from packet labels the class has collected. Close by running through the five can-dos of the self-assessment with the group's own measures.
generation_prompt: Build a class measuring record tool on a fixed 1600x900 SVG stage. A record chart with a row for each child of a group of five holds a long jump, a school bag's weight and a drink of water. A deep blue record card takes a measure, and a Flip button turns it through three forms, two units, the smallest unit and a decimal in the larger unit, each green with a violet unit fact beside it and grey zeros holding places. Rows are dragged into ascending order once every measure is in one unit, the moving row amber. Weights are added in the smallest unit and written back in the larger unit in green. A measuring jug marked in millilitres pours each drink, which is read off its marks and added into litres and millilitres. Pointer events only, no assets, no network.
